topic: The Great Pyramid's Hidden Voids: What Modern Scans Actually Found
framing_note: The phrase 'oldest cover-up' is unsupported by the sources below. The evidence supports an investigation of documented hidden spaces, construction logistics, worker infrastructure, and unresolved engineering questions. Do not claim a cover-up or deliberate concealment without direct evidence.
discovery_warning: Human reviewer confirmed approval of the six supported claims and contextual source on 2026-11-13. The boat-pit graffiti source is accepted as an interpretive source, but its claim remains excluded from the canonical ledger/script pending a second independent source required by schema validation.

sources.title: Discovery of a big void in Khufu’s Pyramid by observation of cosmic-ray muons
sources.review_anchor: Abstract; pp. 386–390; figures and Extended Data Table 1
sources.candidate_relevance: Reports a large void above the Grand Gallery with a minimum length of 30 metres, observed using three muon detection technologies and independent analyses.
sources.limitations: The paper explicitly says the intended purpose of the void is unknown. Do not label it a chamber, room, tomb, or proof of a cover-up unless the paper directly supports that description.

sources.title: Precise characterization of a corridor-shaped structure in Khufu’s Pyramid by observation of cosmic-ray muons
sources.candidate_relevance: Characterizes the North Face Corridor behind the Chevron using independent Nagoya and CEA muon measurements. The paper estimates a corridor roughly 9 metres long with a cross-section around 2 metres by 2 metres.
sources.limitations: This North Face Corridor is distinct from the 2017 ScanPyramids Big Void. The article discusses possible architectural relevance but does not establish the corridor's original function.

sources.title: Les papyrus de la mer Rouge I. Le journal de Merer
sources.review_anchor: IFAO catalogue entry and the English/Arabic appendices/translations linked from the entry; inspect the published papyrus transcription and translation
sources.candidate_relevance: IFAO describes the Wadi el-Jarf papyri as logbooks from Inspector Merer's team, recording river transport of limestone blocks from Tura quarries to Khufu's Great Pyramid while it was under construction.
sources.limitations: The catalogue description is not a substitute for reading the translated logbook. Reviewer must inspect the underlying text and note the exact papyrus, entry, and page before approving any specific claim.

sources.title: The Lost City of the Pyramids (Heit el-Ghurab)
sources.review_anchor: Project page sections describing the 4th Dynasty settlement, excavation location, area, and site functions
sources.candidate_relevance: AERA reports a 4th Dynasty settlement south of the Sphinx, more than 7 hectares in extent, with workshops, bakeries, warehouses, and administrative spaces. AERA says it served the pyramid complexes of Menkaure and Khafre and probably Khufu.
sources.limitations: The connection to Khufu is explicitly qualified as 'probably'. Do not state that every excavated building housed Great Pyramid builders or that all residents directly worked on Khufu's pyramid.

sources.title: Some Notes on the Graffiti Written on the Cover Stones from the Second Boat Pit of Khufu
sources.publication: Bulletin of the Society for Near Eastern Studies in Japan 59(1), 2–13
sources.review_anchor: Article abstract and full PDF, pp. 2–13; inspect photographs and authors' interpretation of the graffiti
sources.candidate_relevance: Examines ink graffiti on cover stones from Khufu's second boat pit and proposes that markings reflect different stages and organizations involved in moving stones.
sources.limitations: The abstract uses interpretive language such as 'seem' and 'presumed'. Preserve those qualifications and distinguish the authors' interpretation from direct observation.

sources.title: AERA Annual Report 2023–2024: The Great Pyramid Scanning Project
sources.review_anchor: AERA Annual Report 2023–2024, printed pp. 8–9 (corrected; not p. 7).
sources.candidate_relevance: Describes systematic recording of bedrock features around Khufu's pyramid, including postholes, lever sockets, quarry channels, and builders' marks over a large area.
sources.limitations: This is an annual fieldwork report describing an ongoing recording project, not a final comprehensive reconstruction of the building method. Do not turn preliminary observations into settled conclusions.

sources.title: The Great Pyramid
sources.authors: Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities
sources.review_anchor: Official monument page, main descriptive text
sources.candidate_relevance: Provides official baseline description: association with King Khufu, reported original height, known chambers, casing stones, boats, and a stated estimated construction period.
sources.limitations: Use only for baseline context. The page's 10–20 year construction estimate is an estimate, not a directly observed duration. It also says the exact construction method is not entirely certain.

candidate_claims.text: Muon radiography identified a large void above the Great Gallery with a minimum length of 30 metres, and three different muon detection technologies independently supported its detection.
candidate_claims.reviewer_notes: Verify the abstract, figure descriptions, and measurement qualifications in the original paper.

candidate_claims.text: A separate corridor-shaped void behind the North Face Chevron was characterized at roughly 9 metres long and about 2 metres by 2 metres in cross-section.
candidate_claims.reviewer_notes: Check Table 1 and distinguish this North Face Corridor from the 2017 Big Void.

candidate_claims.text: The Wadi el-Jarf logbooks published by Pierre Tallet record Inspector Merer's team transporting limestone from Tura to Khufu's pyramid construction site.
candidate_claims.reviewer_notes: Read the actual papyrus transcription/translation and record the exact papyrus and entry before approval.

candidate_claims.text: Excavations at Heit el-Ghurab uncovered a 4th Dynasty settlement with workshops, bakeries, warehouses, and administrative spaces; AERA links it to the Giza pyramid complexes and says its role for Khufu is probable.
candidate_claims.reviewer_notes: Keep AERA's qualification 'probably Khufu'; verify the site chronology and the wording on the project record.

candidate_claims.text: A study of graffiti on Khufu's second boat-pit cover stones interprets the markings as evidence of different stages and organizations in stone transport.
candidate_claims.reviewer_notes: Human reviewer retains this as DEBATED/interpretive. The current canonical validator requires at least two distinct approved source records for DEBATED claims; only one source is currently linked. Do not script until independently corroborated.

candidate_claims.text: AERA's ongoing survey documents construction-related features in bedrock around Khufu's pyramid, including postholes, lever sockets, and quarry channels.
candidate_claims.reviewer_notes: Confirm printed report page 7 and describe this as an ongoing survey, not a complete explanation of the construction method.

unsupported_or_prohibited_framing.text: The Great Pyramid was part of an ancient cover-up or deliberate suppression of evidence.
unsupported_or_prohibited_framing.reason: None of the reviewed source records establishes a cover-up, intentional suppression, or conspiracy. Do not use as a factual narration hook.

unsupported_or_prohibited_framing.text: The Big Void is a hidden chamber, treasure room, or secret tomb.
unsupported_or_prohibited_framing.reason: The 2017 Nature paper reports a void and explicitly states that its intended purpose is unknown.

unsupported_or_prohibited_framing.text: Archaeologists know exactly how the Great Pyramid was built.
unsupported_or_prohibited_framing.reason: The Egyptian Ministry page and the research literature describe remaining uncertainty about the precise construction method.

reviewer_instructions: Open every original source URL and confirm the record.
Read the cited section, abstract, table, page, or papyrus translation rather than relying on search snippets.
Record an exact page, section, table, papyrus identifier, or catalogue number for each approved source.
Mark each source APPROVED or REJECTED only after inspection; leave all others UNREVIEWED.
Only add a claim to data/evidence_ledger.json after its supporting source records are approved and the exact claim is checked.
Use DEBATED for interpretations or live scholarly disagreement, and UNKNOWN when the evidence does not establish an answer.
Do not add claims about aliens, lost advanced technology, secret chambers, or a cover-up unless direct, inspectable evidence supports them.

human_review.decision: Approved six supported claims and the official monument source for context; boat-pit graffiti remains debated and excluded pending independent corroboration.
human_review.basis: Reviewer explicitly confirmed: 'Yes' to having reviewed the cited source material and approving the six recommended Great Pyramid claims, with boat-pit graffiti remaining DEBATED.
